description: Designer designing a TUI file manager adapts web UI patterns without translating to terminal medium
prompt: I'm designing a TUI file manager. I want a hover state that shows a tooltip with file metadata when the user moves the cursor over a filename. I also want to use flexbox-style layout so the panels resize fluidly.
trap: Applies web UI patterns (hover state, flexbox) to TUI without acknowledging that the terminal medium has no hover state (focus is binary: has focus or doesn't) and no pixel-level fluid layout (all positioning is integer character-cell arithmetic).
expectations: Should explain that hover state does not exist in terminal keyboard-first interaction — focus is binary, not positional-cursor-over-element
Should explain that TUI layout uses integer character-cell arithmetic, not CSS flexbox or pixel-based fluid layout

Should suggest a keyboard-driven alternative to hover tooltips: showing file metadata in a fixed detail panel or status bar when the file has keyboard focus (highlighted row / cursor position = focus)
Should address how to show file metadata without hover: detail panel on the right, or status bar at the bottom showing selected file's metadata
Should NOT design hover-based interactions without translation to the terminal medium
negative_expectations: Should NOT suggest implementing CSS-style flexible box layout in a terminal without explaining the integer-cell constraint
Should NOT design hover-tooltip behavior as if it transfers directly from web UI

description: Designer designing a TUI without addressing key binding discoverability
prompt: I'm designing a TUI dashboard showing system metrics. The user can switch between views (CPU, memory, network, disk), filter by time range, and export data. Design the key binding scheme.
trap: Produces a key binding map without designing the discoverability mechanism — the status bar, help overlay, and mode indicator. A key binding scheme with no discoverability mechanism produces a TUI where users must guess or read documentation to use the tool.
expectations: Should produce a key binding map organized by context (navigation, filter mode, export mode, global)
Should specify what the status bar shows in each context — at minimum '? = help' and the 2-3 most relevant bindings for current focus
Should design a '?' help overlay showing the complete key binding map
Should address how mode is communicated visually when filter mode or export mode is active (status bar indicator)
Should follow keyboard conventions: arrow keys and/or j/k for navigation, Tab for panel/view switching, Escape to cancel/go back, q to quit
Should address terminal-reserved bindings (Ctrl-C = interrupt must still work)
negative_expectations: Should NOT produce a key binding map without specifying how those bindings are discoverable to a first-time user
Should NOT assign bindings to Ctrl-C without providing an alternative quit mechanism
Should NOT design the key binding scheme as if users will read external documentation to discover it

description: Designer specifying TUI color strategy without addressing NO_COLOR and non-color signals
prompt: I want to use color to communicate pod status in a Kubernetes dashboard TUI: green for running, yellow for pending, red for failed, gray for unknown.
trap: Designs color as the only signal for pod status without specifying non-color alternatives. Fails for color-blind users, NO_COLOR environments, and monochrome terminals — the design produces a tool where state is invisible without color.
expectations: Should accept color as an enhancement but require non-color primary signals
Should specify text or symbol signals paired with color: e.g., '✓ Running', '⟳ Pending', '✗ Failed', '? Unknown' — or status text in the row itself
Should specify NO_COLOR behavior: when NO_COLOR is set, what remains to communicate pod status (the text/symbol signals)
Should use semantic color tokens rather than literal green/yellow/red/gray: 'success-indicator', 'warning-indicator', 'error-indicator', 'muted' mapped to 16 ANSI colors
Should address that the terminal's ANSI color values are controlled by the user's terminal theme — design must work in both dark and light terminal backgrounds
negative_expectations: Should NOT design a color scheme where color is the only distinguishing signal for pod state
Should NOT use literal RGB or hex color values as the primary color specification without semantic token layer
Should NOT ignore the NO_COLOR environment variable requirement

description: Designer designing a full-screen TUI without specifying the focus model and modal overlay behavior
prompt: My TUI has a main list panel and a detail panel on the right. When the user presses 'e', it should open a modal dialog to edit the selected item. Design the focus behavior.
trap: Describes the modal opening without specifying: how focus is communicated visually in the list panel and detail panel, what focus-trap behavior the modal must enforce, how Escape closes the modal, and what happens to focus after the modal closes.
expectations: Should specify how the list panel communicates selection/focus: highlighted row (reverse video), cursor position, optional ▶ marker
Should specify how the detail panel shows it is active vs inactive: border style or color change (bright border when active, dim when inactive)
Should specify the modal focus-trap: while the modal is open, Tab and panel-switching bindings must not move focus outside the modal
Should specify modal close behavior: Escape closes the modal without saving, returns focus to the list at the same selected item
Should specify what happens if the user presses 'e' when no item is selected (disabled state — no modal opens)
Should address what 'Edit' modal's focus model is internally: which input field has focus on open, how Tab traverses fields within the modal
negative_expectations: Should NOT describe modal opening without specifying the focus-trap behavior during modal
Should NOT leave focus return path after modal close unspecified
Should NOT omit the visual focus indicator design for the list panel and detail panel

description: Designer not addressing TUI layout at 80x24 minimum terminal size
prompt: I'm designing a TUI with four panels: a navigation sidebar (20 columns), a main content area, a detail panel (40 columns), and a status panel at the bottom. The status panel should be 8 rows tall.
trap: Accepts a panel layout without pressure-testing it at 80x24 — the standard minimum terminal size. Four panels with the specified sizes do not fit in 80x24, producing a broken layout for any user running a default terminal.
expectations: Should calculate whether the proposed layout fits at 80x24: 20 (sidebar) + content + 40 (detail) = requires content area to be 80-20-40-2 (borders) = 18 columns, which may be insufficient; status panel of 8 rows leaves only 16 rows for content panels
Should identify that the layout needs a responsive fallback for 80x24: which panels collapse or hide at minimum size
Should propose a breakpoint strategy: at narrow widths, collapse the detail panel (accessible via drill-down or a key); at very narrow widths (≤60 columns), collapse the sidebar too
Should specify what appears at 80x24 vs at a wider terminal (e.g., 120+ columns)
Should specify when the 'terminal too small' message appears (below the minimum functional size)
Should note that the 8-row status panel is unusual — most TUI status bars are 1-2 rows; clarify whether this is intended and if so, what it contains
negative_expectations: Should NOT accept the proposed layout without checking if it fits at 80x24
Should NOT design a TUI with no responsive strategy for minimum terminal size
Should NOT omit a 'terminal too small' fallback state
